A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAPM study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and fine-tuning evaluations, benchmark leakage analyses, RAPM results, and retrieval-component ablations in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds metric-validation, retrieval-confidence, Prot2Text, and structural-retrieval results.

M1.justification: RAPM retains sequence/embedding dual indexing, feature aggregation, similarity weighting with alpha = 0.5, confidence-tagged retrieval, and few-shot prompting. The new FoldSeek experiments compare retrieval alternatives; they do not establish a structural component added to RAPM.

E1.justification: v4 adds Prot2Text functional-description evaluation and leakage analysis, plus structural-input retrieval comparisons. It also reports incorporating Swiss-Prot captioning into the unified OOD instruction benchmark, although separate OOD captioning results and sample counts are absent. The original protein-understanding tasks remain.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 3 remain unchanged. Appendix A adds a RAPM comparison against Prot2Text_BASE and introduces FoldSeek and FoldSeek+MMSeqs2 alongside sequence and embedding retrieval in Table 8.

E3.justification: v4 adds entity-set F1 and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocols, groups results by average retrieval-similarity intervals, and describes converting captioning annotations into instructions. Existing split-construction commands and fine-tuning/inference hyperparameters are retained. The new joint-training/testing statement alone does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds validation of Entity-BLEU against entity F1 and LLM judgments. Section 5.4 adds performance analysis across retrieval-confidence levels, while Appendix A examines structural versus sequence retrieval and Figure 3 extends leakage analysis to Prot2Text. These substantially expand the questions investigated beyond the retained retrieval-count, indexing, and prompting ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Pearson correlation already appears in Figure 4 in v1; v4 adds correlations for another analysis without introducing a different statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces substantial retrieval results: Function E-BLEU changes from 45.2 to 11.9 for MMSeqs2 and from 39.9 to 10.8 for ESM-2, while the fine-tuned and RAPM rows remain unchanged. The older retrieval E-BLEU values reappear in v4 Table 8 without clearly distinguished settings, preventing interpretation as same-setting losses. New metric-validation, confidence, Prot2Text, structural-retrieval, and leakage results substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The retrieval, feature-aggregation, HNSW, and Entity-BLEU mathematics are retained. The added F1 and judge-scoring formulas state standard entity-set overlap calculations for evaluation; no substantive theoretical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about benchmark leakage, inadequate text-overlap metrics, retrieval competitiveness, and RAPM's benefits. Explicitly naming the benchmark and metric in v4's contribution list restates contributions already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v4 tentatively attributes label leakage to protein annotation practices, interprets metric correlations as support for the entity database, discusses performance with low-confidence retrieval, and argues that structural information complements sequence retrieval. The original limitations and principal interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New disclosures include the judge prompt, joint training/testing with separate task reporting, PEER as a listed annotation source, and local-execution capabilities in Table 9. Hardware, training duration, optimization settings, inference parameters, and the code/data access link remain unchanged. The judge model and several new experimental settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Gu et al. (2024), Ma et al. (2024), Xu et al. (2022, PEER), and Xue et al. (2022), and expands discussion of the already-cited Prot2Text work. The overall positioning of retrieval and RAPM relative to protein language models is retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language corrections, renames the OOD benchmark, revises the contribution bullet, updates author information, and adds acknowledgments. It inserts a metric-analysis section and three appendices, renumbering retained material, while preserving most existing prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds dedicated tables for metric validation, confidence levels, Prot2Text, retrieval modalities, and resource/capability comparisons, plus a boxed judge prompt. Figure 2 is redrawn and Figure 3 gains Prot2Text leakage rows. Existing plots and several tables are resized or relocated, substantially expanding the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The added metric-validation and retrieval-confidence analyses, together with Prot2Text and structural-retrieval comparisons, provide useful checks absent from v1 and modestly strengthen empirical support. The gains are limited by incomplete captioning and judge-evaluation documentation and the unclear relationship between the revised Table 3 retrieval scores and older values retained in Table 8.
